nodes.name: Bosnian pine
nodes.desc: A tough high-mountain pine that reaches the alpine tree line. Baikushev's pine in Pirin is estimated to be over 1,300 years old, Bulgaria's oldest tree.

nodes.name: Macedonian pine
nodes.desc: One of the park's largest forest types, covering roughly 54 square kilometres of the mountain slopes.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: A low berry shrub of mountain forest floors and clearings, whose fruit is eaten by birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Alpine grasses and herbs
nodes.desc: The high meadows above the tree line, where the park's 1,315 plant species include many endemics. Chamois graze them in summer.

nodes.name: Balkan chamois
nodes.desc: A sure-footed goat-antelope of steep rock. It grazes alpine herbs in summer and shifts to conifers in winter, and is among the park's most valued mammals.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: A small woodland deer that browses leaves, shoots and berries in the park's forests.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: A large grazer and browser of forest and meadow, listed among the park's mammals of highest conservation value.

nodes.name: European snow vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of rocky alpine slopes that feeds on plants. It is common prey for birds of prey and small carnivores.

nodes.name: Red squirrel
nodes.desc: A tree-living rodent that feeds largely on conifer seeds and cones, and is recorded in the park area.

nodes.name: Eurasian nutcracker
nodes.desc: A mountain-forest crow that feeds on pine seeds and hoards them, helping spread conifers.

nodes.name: Beech marten
nodes.desc: An agile omnivorous hunter that takes small mammals, birds and fruit. The nearby pine marten is also on the park list.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: A widespread raptor that hunts small mammals such as voles, and also takes birds and reptiles.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever scavenger that feeds on carcasses left by larger predators, as well as on small prey.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: A pack hunter that across Eurasia takes mainly red deer, roe deer and wild boar, and is on the park's species list.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that gets most of its energy from plants such as berries and pine cones, and also eats carrion and some prey. Bulgaria holds several hundred.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A powerful raptor with only a few breeding pairs in the park; chamois are among its possible prey.

nodes.name: Snow cover
nodes.desc: Snow lies about 120 to 160 days a year at high elevation, feeding the meadows and lakes with meltwater.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Energy for all plant growth, strongest on the open alpine slopes.

nodes.name: Glacial lakes
nodes.desc: The park has 118 glacial lakes, and Snezhnika, Europe's southernmost glacier, still survives.

nodes.name: Mountain soil
nodes.desc: Thin soils and decayed matter supply nutrients to forests and meadows.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates break down dead wood, needles and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
